To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Wong formula can be generalized to reproduce quantal results for fusion cross sections of light symmetric systems, and that the coupled-channels calculation including low-lying collective excitations can reproduce the subbarrier fusion cross sections of $^{58}\mathrm{Ni} + ^{58}\mathrm{ Ni}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ca} + ^{58} \mathrm{Ni}$ systems.

(1) a generalized Wong formula can reproduce fusion cross sections for light symmetric systems, and (2) the subbarrier fusion cross sections for the $^{58}$N+$^{58}$N and $^{40}Ca+^{58}$Ni system are well reproduced by a semi-microscopics modeling of the coupled-channels method.

we have developed an analytical formula for the fusion cross sections, which reproduces results practically indistinguishble from a full quantam calculation, even for systems with an oscillatory behavior of fusion cross sections, and we have developed a semi-microscopical modeling of heavy-ion reactions, which combine a coupled-channels approach with state-of-the-art structure calculations for collective motions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of heavy-ion fusion cross sections at energies around the barrier.
the understanding of the fusion reactions in terms of the underlying nuclear structure.
the microscopic modeling of the nuclear fusion reactions, with the aim to understand the reaction mechanisms in terms of the nuclear structure properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy-ion fusion reactions are well understood in the energy region around the Coulomb barriers.

the fusion reaction is an interesting and challenging field of study, and that the fusion reaction will continue to provide new and important insights into nuclear structure, and will continue to be the subject of intense theoretical and experimental investigations.

, in spite of the fact that fusion reactions are still far from being understood completely, the current theoretical developments have reached a level that allows us to predict the fusion cross sections with a precision comparable to the experimental accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a semi-microscopically based coupled-channels calculation is able to reproduce experimental fusion data at energies below the Coulomb barrier, and that it is a promising tool to study fusion reaction dynamics in the sub-barrier energy region.

the semi-microscopic coupled-channels model can be a powerful tool to describe heavy-ion fusion reactions with a good accuracy, especially when the fusion is dominated by the low-lying collective modes.

the Wong formula is useful for practical applications to heavy-ion fusion reactions even for light systems, and that a semi-microscopics model is useful for a quantitative description of fusion reactions of heavy systems, which are not well described by the Wong formula.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple modification of the barrier parameters of the Wong formula is able to reproduce fusion cross sections at energies below the barrier.
the anharmonicity plays a crucial role in the fusion enhancement observed in these systems.
the semi-microscopic approach is a promising tool for a systematic study of heavy-ion fusion reaction at energies around the barrier.
